name: Indonesia
summary: Southeast Asian archipelago of over 17,000 islands, site of one of the deadliest covert operations of the Cold War—the 1965–1966 slaughter of 500,000 to 1,000,000 leftists, unionists, and civilians supported by the CIA and US Embassy.
historical_context: Following independence under anti-colonial leader President Sukarno, Indonesia was a founder of the Non-Aligned Movement (Bandung Conference 1955). Sukarno pursued nationalist economic policies, expropriated Western oil and rubber holdings, and maintained a domestic political alliance with the Communist Party of Indonesia (PKI), the largest non-ruling communist party in the world with 3 million members. Beginning in October 1965, the Indonesian military under Major General Suharto seized power following a murky failed coup. Declassified CIA and State Department files prove that US officials furnished covert radio communications equipment, small arms, cash, and intelligence lists containing thousands of names of PKI leaders to the Indonesian military and death squads, who systematically hunted down, tortured, and slaughtered an estimated 500,000 to 1,000,000 people. General Suharto established a 32-year Western-backed military dictatorship (the 'New Order'), opening the country's vast mineral and oil resources to American multinationals.
primary_institutions_involved: United States Department of State (Embassy in Jakarta)
Western-backed anticommunist death squads (Ansor / Pemuda Pancasila)
